subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: Should OpenClaw allow a bounded per-reviewer-instance exact-input cache for low-risk model-backed exec reviewer verdicts, and is node/gateway scope enough while plugin helper reuse remains separate?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the fix changes one-request-one-review semantics on the exec approval boundary, so cache lifetime, key shape, and sibling-surface scope need maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve bounded exact-input memo
options.body: Accept a per-reviewer-instance memo keyed by the full reviewed input after the linked PR provides real configured-run proof.

options.title: Require broader host coverage
options.body: Block the fix until plugin helper or codex-app-server reviewer lifetime is explicitly reused or declared out of scope.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Reject caching and accept repeated model cost so each exec request receives a fresh model-backed review.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded exact-input memo
recommendation.body: Accept a per-reviewer-instance memo keyed by the full reviewed input after the linked PR provides real configured-run proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the normalized exec auto-reviewer behavior and is the strongest history-backed owner for the approval-boundary semantics.
